key_insight: A simple generative model learns protein sequences, structures, and functional context together. This enables protein design aimed at specific molecular functions and multiple structural states.
problem_solved: Designing proteins requires more than producing a plausible sequence or a single structure: the design must also support the intended function and potentially different structural states.
method: Jointly learn protein sequence and structure within a generative model.
Incorporate functional context to guide designs toward specified molecular functions.
Represent multiple structural states rather than focusing only on a single conformation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this illustrates how jointly modeling related biological information can support more function-directed generation. It points toward protein design tools that account for structural flexibility as well as sequence.
visual_elements: Three connected icons labeled sequence, structure, and function feeding into one generative model.
A design pipeline showing a requested molecular function leading to a generated protein.
One protein illustrated in multiple structural states with arrows connecting them.
A comparison panel contrasting single-structure design with function-aware, multi-state design.
